tailMarker.anomalyNote: Resolved, no anomaly fired. The marker is a colorant, not a fragrance or preservative - section 3.1 includes any CI colorant in the tail class and takes the earliest member, so CI 17200 at rank 7 governs (PHENOXYETHANOL is at 13, PARFUM last at 30). Rank 7 is above the 'rank <= 3' cut and three conditioning ingredients precede it. The consequence is a six-entry above-tail segment and, most importantly, GLYCOLIC ACID at rank 29 - the second-to-last entry in a thirty-entry list. The product's entire acid-gloss identity rests on a sub-1% claim carrier, and R6a therefore contributes nothing here (it requires the acid above the tail).

COCAMIDOPROPYL BETAINE (3) explicitly not counted toward S1: it is an amphoteric co-surfactant, not a substantive cationic conditioning agent (lexicon family 1 covers quats, esterquats and amidoamines only)
S2 satisfied: CETEARYL ALCOHOL at rank 2, immediately after AQUA
S3 not satisfied: zero non-fatty-alcohol lipids above the tail. AMODIMETHICONE (6) is an R2 silicone; COCOS NUCIFERA OIL (9) is tail-side
Not counted (tail-side): HYDROXYPROPYL GUAR (11), POLYQUATERNIUM-37 (17), PROPYLENE GLYCOL DICAPRYLATE/DICAPRATE (21), ACRYLATES/STEARYL METHACRYLATE COPOLYMER (23)

thresholdReasoning: Why moderate, not high: high requires >= 2 signals; only S2 fires.
Why moderate, not low: low requires none of the three, and S2 is satisfied. 'Exactly one satisfied signal' is explicitly moderate.

This is the structurally minimal formula the lexicon describes for this product family: above the tail there is water, a fatty alcohol, an amphoteric surfactant, one quat, a glycol and one amino silicone.

SODIUM CHLORIDE (10), ETHANOLAMINE (15), the trideceth/sorbitan/acrylates block and EDTA (27) are family-10 infrastructure with zero credit
A short above-tail section is evidence that little can be inferred, not evidence of a weak product (lexicon family 12)
limitations: Section 9.1's honest limitation applies with force on a six-entry above-tail segment.

Confidence moderate, not high: the route separation is unambiguous, but the above-tail care base is thin (four substantive entries) and PROPYLENE GLYCOL (5) is the only humectant-class species above the tail, so calling the architecture 'coherent' is a judgment on a minimal segment.

COCAMIDOPROPYL BETAINE (3) at rank 3 in a rinse-out mask is unusual; treated as a co-surfactant with no care credit

primaryFocus.evidenceScope: Above-tail architecture plus the section 9.5.2 hierarchy and the section 9.5.4 three-criterion shine threshold; product positioning used strictly as corroboration.
primaryFocus.rationale: All special-purpose routes fail and the humectant cluster fails; the shine threshold then clears on all three criteria - an alignment-oriented amino silicone above the tail, a genuinely low lipid load, and exact-product Gloss/Laminierung positioning as corroboration. evidenceSignals: Step 3 repair fails: no R5, no bond token
Step 3 curl_support fails: one cationic above the tail, both cationic polymers tail-side, no curl positioning
Step 3 color_care fails: the CI colorants are product colorants, not an anti-fade candidate; no colour-protection positioning. An acid/chelator is explicitly not anti-fade proof

Step 4 moisture fails: PROPYLENE GLYCOL (5) is the only R9 humectant above the tail - cluster size 1 against a required 3. CAPRYLYL GLYCOL (22) is a preservative booster to be discounted by default and is tail-side anyway

Step 5 shine criterion 1 satisfied: AMODIMETHICONE (6) is an alignment-oriented R2 amino silicone above the tail, and the lipid load is comparatively low - there is no R4b heavy lipid above the tail, indeed no lipid at all. This is the formula shape section 9.5.4 describes as distinguishing a gloss product from a rich nourishing mask
Step 5 shine criterion 2: the optical route is a distinct deposition species rather than the M1 cationic/fatty-alcohol film itself - the marginal leg, see thresholdReasoning
Step 5 shine criterion 3 satisfied: exact-product Gloss / Laminierung positioning is visible in the product name and directions - corroboration only
R6a: GLYCOLIC ACID (29) is below the marker, so the acid-gloss context contributes nothing. R6a is supporting context and never sufficient in any case
primaryFocus.derivation: Section 9.5.2 steps 1-5 in order, with section 9.5.4's three criteria applied in full. focus_care_verdict = not_applicable (the chosen focus is not a repair/moisture decision). claim_role = corroborating.
thresholdReasoning: Why shine, not smoothing: criterion 1's low-lipid-load conjunct is the discriminator the standard names, and it is satisfied here as clearly as it is falsified on packet 06 (which has shea butter and coconut oil above the tail and therefore takes smoothing instead). The two products form a clean pair on that test.

Why shine, not general: all three criteria clear. The standard's open question 6 asks whether the gloss cohort actually clears the three-criterion threshold on real INCIs, or whether the low-lipid-load criterion excludes products the charter wants classified as shine-focused. On this product the answer is that it clears - and it clears because the formula is lipid-free above the tail, not because of the acid.

Why criterion 2 is the marginal leg: the base film here is cetearyl alcohol plus one quat, and the amodimethicone is a separate deposition species with a documented preferential-deposition behaviour, so I judged the optical route not to be merely the smoothing film already counted. A stricter reader could hold that M3 here just shares M1, in which case section 6 rule 2 sends this to smoothing with the gloss claim kept as claim context only. That is the adjacent call and the reason for moderate confidence.

Corroboration discipline: criterion 3 was satisfied by positioning, and positioning can never create the route. I confirmed criteria 1 and 2 on architecture first and used the claim only to complete the third leg, exactly as section 9.5.2 step 9 requires.
counterSignals: Glycolic acid temporarily plasticizes the fibre (a measured decrease in Young's modulus). It does not seal, coat, close the cuticle, laminate, or produce lasting change - and at rank 29 it contributes nothing structurally here regardless
'Lamination' is positioning, not distinct chemistry; there is no lamination property and none was created
The source directions use 'versiegeln'; that wording is banned in this record and in any downstream copy
The optical mechanism behind gloss is not separable from ordinary smoothing-film shine, which is why criterion 1's architecture test rather than the claim had to carry the decision
limitations: Confidence moderate: criterion 2 is a judgment call, and the whole shine reading rests on a single silicone species at rank 6 of a six-entry above-tail segment.

Independence note: the standard's sections 9.3 and 18 and the lexicon's worked examples discuss this product family by name. My reading of criteria 1-3 is my own, but the packet was not read in ignorance of those examples - see blind-notes.

assumptionNotes: Tail marker taken as CI 17200/RED 33 (7), the earliest tail-class member. Colorants are a tail class under section 3.1. This gives a six-entry above-tail segment and places GLYCOLIC ACID (29) far below the marker.
COCAMIDOPROPYL BETAINE (3) treated as an amphoteric co-surfactant with no cationic-conditioning credit; it is not in lexicon family 1.
AMODIMETHICONE counted as an alignment-oriented R2 silicone for the shine criterion-1 architecture, and explicitly never as bond chemistry or as a repair upgrader.
CAPRYLYL GLYCOL (22) discounted from any humectant cluster by default as a near-always antimicrobial booster (lexicon family 7); tail-side in any case.
PROPYLENE GLYCOL (5) counted as an R9 humectant above the tail, but as a single member it establishes nothing under the D5 guard.
Root-to-tip application in the directions treated as a P5 protocol deviation that fires the root/scalp review trigger, without changing R8 or creating a scalp property.

Review triggers I would fire: gloss_lamination_claim (charter F4 - verify the shine threshold was met independently and the banned wording is absent); root/scalp application (inherited Conditioner trigger, per the R8 mask delta). No bond_claim_review, no protein_payload_review, no tail_marker_anomaly.

Claims: I had no claims summary, but the product NAME and the directions text carry unambiguous Gloss/Laminierung positioning, and section 9.5.4 criterion 3 permits exactly that as corroboration. This is the one product where positioning legitimately entered a value - as the third leg of a threshold whose first two legs were satisfied on architecture alone.

Independence caveat: this product family is named as a worked example in the standard (section 9.3, section 18 open question 6) and in the evidence lexicon (family 8, D-3). I could not un-read those, and I have flagged it in blind-notes rather than pretending the read was clean.
